units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Yes.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Your word of honour?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Sits down .
Yes.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Rises .
Arthur, let me see for myself.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: No, no.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: If there is no one there why should I not look in that room? Arthur, you must let me go into that room and satisfy myself. Let me know that no eavesdropper has heard my life’s secret. Arthur, you don’t realise what I am going through.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Robert, this must stop. I have told you that there is no one in that room—that is enough.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Rushes to the door of the room .
It is not enough. I insist on going into this room. You have told me there is no one there, so what reason can you have for refusing me?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: For God’s sake, don’t! There is some one there. Some one whom you must not see.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Ah, I thought so!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: I forbid you to enter that room.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Stand back. My life is at stake. And I don’t care who is there. I will know who it is to whom I have told my secret and my shame.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Enters room .
Great heavens! his own wife!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN comes back , with a look of scorn and anger on his face .
What explanation have you to give me for the presence of that woman here?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Robert, I swear to you on my honour that that lady is stainless and guiltless of all offence towards you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: She is a vile, an infamous thing!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Don’t say that, Robert! It was for your sake she came here. It was to try and save you she came here. She loves you and no one else.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: You are mad. What have I to do with her intrigues with you? Let her remain your mistress! You are well suited to each other. She, corrupt and shameful—you, false as a friend, treacherous as an enemy even—
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: It is not true, Robert. Before heaven, it is not true. In her presence and in yours I will explain all.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Let me pass, sir. You have lied enough upon your word of honour.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN goes out .
LORD GORING rushes to the door of the drawing-room , when MRS. CHEVELEY comes out , looking radiant and much amused .
With a mock curtsey.
Good evening, Lord Goring!
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Mrs. Cheveley! Great heavens! . . . May I ask what you were doing in my drawing-room?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Merely listening. I have a perfect passion for listening through keyholes. One always hears such wonderful things through them.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Doesn’t that sound rather like tempting Providence?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Oh! surely Providence can resist temptation by this time.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Makes a sign to him to take her cloak off , which he does .
I am glad you have called. I am going to give you some good advice.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Oh! pray don’t. One should never give a woman anything that she can’t wear in the evening.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I see you are quite as wilful as you used to be.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Far more! I have greatly improved. I have had more experience.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Too much experience is a dangerous thing. Pray have a cigarette. Half the pretty women in London smoke cigarettes. Personally I prefer the other half.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Thanks. I never smoke. My dressmaker wouldn’t like it, and a woman’s first duty in life is to her dressmaker, isn’t it? What the second duty is, no one has as yet discovered.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: You have come here to sell me Robert Chiltern’s letter, haven’t you?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: To offer it to you on conditions. How did you guess that?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Because you haven’t mentioned the subject. Have you got it with you?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Sitting down .
Oh, no! A well-made dress has no pockets.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: What is your price for it?
units.name: LORD GORING
